payload.notes: Coordinates A, B, C, V are program-owned and not redefined; the program inserts them at the start of tikzpicture, so this document will only compile once that insertion happens. I checked the program frame against the pixel measurements: A-V x-span 3.751 units (236.3 px x 0.015873) and V-B y-span 3.747 units match the pixel distances. The only literal coordinate is the free left endpoint (-4.151,-1.860), derived from pixel x=23 with the same frame and y equal to V's y. Edges: horizontal line drawn as L--V--A to keep the small V-to-A offset (y -1.860 vs -1.863), B--V, and A--C as required named edges. No right-angle mark, since none was verified. Stroke 1.3pt with round joins and 13/15.6 pt labels per STYLE METRICS. Label placements follow the instruction: A right, B above, C left, V below.

Added the upper semicircular arc centred at V (radius 3.744 = 235.79 px * 0.015873), drawn as an arc from the left end through B to the right side, not a full circle. L is moved to V shifted by -R, i.e. (-4.067,-1.860), so the diameter L-V-A and the arc share the same left endpoint. The critic suggested L at (-4.078,-1.861); I followed the instruction's R (3.744) instead. Measured V-to-A distance is about 3.751 and V-to-B about 3.747, so R is within measurement noise. The arc ends at V+(R,0), about 0.007 units short of the program-defined A; this is negligible. A, B, C, V coordinate definitions were omitted because the program inserts them. Labels, bindings, font and line width are unchanged. No right-angle mark added.
